headline: Record Derby Week lifts every segment
summary_short: Churchill Downs' Q2 2026 GAAP revenue rose 4.9% y/y to $980 million on a record-breaking Kentucky Derby Week, with net income up 11.1% y/y to $241 million and diluted EPS of $3.42 (+14.4% y/y), while the company's own Adjusted EBITDA grew $26 million y/y to $477 million.
summary_long: Revenue grew 4.9% y/y to $980M as a record-breaking Derby Week lifted all three segments: Live and Historical Racing (+$34M), Wagering Services and Solutions (+$10M), and Gaming (+$4M). Operating income rose 9.5% y/y to $358M on the same Derby-driven strength plus non-recurrence of a prior-year Virginia HRM impairment. Net income increased 11.1% y/y to $241M, aided by higher equity income from unconsolidated affiliates and lower interest expense. Long-term debt fell 15.5% q/q to $4.11B on Revolver and Term Loan paydowns, while short-term debt jumped to $663M as the $600M 2027 Senior Notes moved into current maturities. The company reaffirmed FY2026 project capital (Rockingham Grand Casino, Victory Run) at $180-220M; no revenue/EPS guidance was given in this filing.

EPS growth of 13.6% outpaced net income growth of 11.1% because weighted-average basic shares fell from 72M to 70M y/y.

Revolver balance fell $328M and Term Loan A fell $30M since year-end per the company's own debt schedule; the $600M 2027 Senior Notes also moved out of the long-term line into current maturities as they are now due within twelve months.

The jump to $663M in current maturities is explained by the $600M 2027 Senior Notes becoming due within twelve months and reclassifying from long-term to current, per the company's own debt maturity schedule; the release does not use the word 'reclassified' explicitly.

The $245M q/q increase in equity is arithmetic: net income of $241M for the quarter was added directly to retained earnings per the statement of shareholders' equity, with a small additional contribution from stock-based compensation.
The filing's MD&A repeatedly anchors the quarter's growth across revenue, operating income, and Adjusted EBITDA to a single cause: a record-breaking Kentucky Derby Week at Churchill Downs Racetrack.
